intendedRegression.summary: Release 2.14 introduced two defects: (1) webhooks/retry.py is_retryable returns True for every status >= 400, so permanent 4xx responses (e.g. 410 Gone) are retried up to the attempt cap; (2) Dispatcher.enqueue always creates a new delivery, so the at-least-once event bus republishing an event produces a second delivery to the same endpoint.
intendedRegression.demonstratedBy: tests/test_dispatcher.py::test_gone_endpoint_is_not_retried and ::test_republished_event_is_delivered_once fail on the shipped code; the other 10 provided tests pass.

permittedFixes: Any correct retry classification: explicit transient set, explicit permanent set, or range checks with 408/429 exceptions
Deduplicate on (event id, endpoint id) in the dispatcher, in the store, or with an index; returning the existing delivery
Retry-After parsing in retry.py, the dispatcher, or a helper, as long as behaviour matches the update
Adding tests under tests/ for the new behaviour
forbiddenShortcuts: Editing the provided tests to weaken assertions (the runner restores them, so this has no effect on results)
Special-casing the statuses or event ids named in the incident instead of fixing the rule
Deduplicating on event id alone (breaks fan-out to multiple endpoints)

clarificationFacts.question: Should 404 be retried? The log shows dlv_8860 got a 404 during a merchant deploy and succeeded on retry.
clarificationFacts.answer: Keep 404 permanent for this hotfix, as the runbook says. Merchants replay from the dashboard. RFC-12 tracks a grace period for deploy-time 404s; call it out in the handoff as a risk rather than changing it here.

clarificationFacts.question: Deduplicate per event, or per event and endpoint?
clarificationFacts.answer: Per event and endpoint. One event fans out to every subscribed endpoint; each is its own delivery.

clarificationFacts.question: If the first delivery failed, should a republish create a new delivery?
clarificationFacts.answer: No. A republish is always a duplicate. Replays go through the dashboard tool, which is out of scope.

clarificationFacts.question: Can I refactor the dispatcher or change the store schema?
clarificationFacts.answer: Keep it a hotfix. A small store change is fine if you explain it; no broad refactor.

requirementUpdate.summary: The partner gateway starts rate limiting: on 429 or 503 with a Retry-After header in whole seconds, schedule the next attempt after that many seconds, capped at MAX_DELAY_SECONDS; otherwise use normal backoff; the attempt cap still applies.
requirementUpdate.delivery: deterministic server milestone via the curveball policy, never randomized per candidate
requirementUpdate.expectedCandidateResponse: acknowledge the update, implement it, add or run a test for it, reflect it in the handoff

expectedOutcomes.greenState: reference and both alternative variants: all 45 non-canary checks pass

knownIssues: Candidate code runs in the same pytest process as trusted tests. The canary test and expected-test-id checks detect reporting tampering, but a determined candidate could still attempt it; such runs are marked indeterminate and routed to human review, never scored as passes.
